persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local stable transcription identifier; source DOI identifies the article.
title: De Marke biorefinery struvite crop-use and relative fertilizer-efficiency observations
citation: Szymańska, M., Szara, E., Wąs, A., Sosulski, T., van Pruissen, G. W. P., & Cornelissen, R. L. (2019). Struvite—An Innovative Fertilizer from Anaerobic Digestate Produced in a Bio-Refinery. Energies, 12(2), 296. https://doi.org/10.3390/en12020296
source_locations: Methods 2.1, article p. 2: nutrient doses and pot setup
Table 1, article p. 6: relative fertilizer efficiency
Results 3.3, article p. 6: explicitly stated apparent nutrient recovery results
geography: Struvite produced at the De Marke experimental dairy farm biorefinery, Hengelo (Gld), the Netherlands; crop pot experiment performed in a greenhouse in Warsaw, Poland
license: The full text states that the article is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license.
material_scope: Dusty mixed recovered struvite precipitated from the liquid fraction of anaerobically digested cattle slurry at a farm-scale Dutch dairy biorefinery. Fertilizer-use experiment grew Lolium multiflorum grass and maize in silty loam and loamy sand soils.
experimental_conditions: Completely randomized greenhouse pot experiment with three replications; each pot contained 15 kg soil. Treatments applied 2.0 g P/pot in all fertilizer treatments; STR supplied 1.17 g N and 1.6 g Mg; STR+N supplied 1.8 g N total (1.17 g from struvite and 0.63 g from ammonium sulfate) and 1.6 g Mg; AP supplied 1.8 g N and no Mg. Potassium was applied uniformly to all pots. Grass was cultivated for 140 days with three mowings; maize was grown for 90 days.
data_scope: 42 records: Table 1 relative N/P fertilizer efficiencies for STR, STR+N and AP across two soils and two crops; 9 nutrient application doses; and 9 apparent N/P recovery values stated explicitly in Results text. Table 1 values are source-calculated relative efficiencies using the commercial AP treatment as 100%; apparent recovery is source-calculated as uptake above the no-N/P control divided by the applied nutrient dose.
limitations: Reference-only; does not represent GreenHub roadside-grass digestate, product production, product acceptance, or market substitution in the project process.
Upstream feedstock for struvite was cattle slurry from a dairy-farm biorefinery, not grass digestate.
The crop study is a controlled greenhouse pot experiment in Polish soils; field-scale fertilizer replacement and Dutch receiving-soil effects are not established.
Relative fertilizer efficiency is not the same as product recovery, nutrient removal from the digestate stream, or guaranteed commercial fertilizer substitution.
Table 1 does not report standard deviations; blank SD fields are not zero. Replicate count comes from the experiment design (n=3).
Two grass apparent-N-recovery values combine STR and STR+N in the source text and are preserved as combined treatments; they must not be split.
Only apparent recovery results stated explicitly in prose were transcribed; graphical bars were not digitized. The record is therefore not a complete per-treatment nutrient-uptake dataset.
Application rates are per pot and cannot be scaled directly to field rates without soil mass, incorporation depth, field calibration, and product-availability assumptions.
No calculation, default, fertilizer credit, or Pareto result consumes this evidence.
conversion_or_processing: Tables and explicit prose values transcribed with original units and conditions. Relative fertilizer efficiency and apparent recovery equations are documented as the article defines them; no scale conversion or graphical digitization performed.
uncertainty: The experiment reports n=3 and statistical group letters for Table 1 but not SD in that table. No uncertainty was inferred for dose or prose-reported recovery values.
